evidence.claim: Contentsquare's engineering blog says ClickHouse is its database of choice to store and serve customer analytics.
Contentsquare documented a real-time ClickHouse architecture with sub-minute freshness requirements and scalability from tens of thousands to 100k+ events per second.
Contentsquare describes Kafka and Flink as important parts of its data pipeline feeding analytical workloads into ClickHouse.
Because ClickHouse is deeply embedded and already meeting important requirements, any VeloDB conversation would need a narrowly defined technical advantage rather than a generic migration pitch.
QuestionPro says it selected ClickHouse after evaluating multiple analytical databases for a system handling billions of rows.
QuestionPro documents a MySQL-to-ClickHouse pipeline using Debezium, Kafka Connect and Kafka with under-one-second transfer latency.
The published architecture powers QuestionPro BI and is designed to give users instant analytical results.
A fair evaluation would need to demonstrate measurable value against an already successful ClickHouse deployment, especially around concurrency, joins, operations, or total cost.
Trino's official user catalog says Razorpay uses Trino with Spark, Hudi, S3 and Hive Metastore to query raw data-lake tables.
Razorpay describes Trino as fast, scalable, SQL-friendly and well integrated with its ecosystem.
If interactive latency, concurrency, or serving-layer efficiency becomes material, an Apache Doris evaluation could be scoped as an acceleration layer rather than assumed as a wholesale replacement.
Trino's official users page says Rapido uses Trino for query federation, data pipelines, KPI/system metrics monitoring and large-dataset analytics.
Rapido's Trino usage supports interactive analysis and visualization with Metabase and Superset.
A serving-layer POC could be relevant only if user-facing or analyst-facing latency/concurrency is demonstrably constrained; current public evidence does not establish that pain.
Vimeo Engineering documented migrating video analytics from Apache Phoenix/HBase to ClickHouse.
Vimeo described real-time analytics spanning more than a billion viewing-log events per day for users ranging from creators to enterprises.
The scale makes the workload technically relevant, but public evidence does not establish dissatisfaction with ClickHouse; any competitive motion must begin with discovery and normalized benchmarks.
